sentences.text: Stomatosuchus was an extinct neosuchian crocodylomorph that reached a length of 10 meters. It possessed a flattened skull with a long, flattened snout filled with small, conical teeth. The jaws featured a lid-like structure lined with these small, conical teeth.
Stomatosuchus inermis is the type and only known species of the genus Stomatosuchus. This animal belongs to the family Stomatosuchidae.
The only known specimen, a large skull collected by Ernst Stromer in Egypt, was destroyed when the Munich Museum was bombed by Allied forces in 1944.
Its skull measured up to 2 meters in length, making it one of the largest known crocodylomorph skulls.

The sole specimen was collected in Egypt in 1911 by the German paleontologist Ernst Stromer. It was delivered to the Munich Museum in 1922 but was destroyed during an Allied bombing raid on April 24–25, 1944.

Researchers suggest the lower jaw of Stomatosuchus may have been toothless and supported a pelican-like throat pouch. The exact diet of Stomatosuchus remains largely unknown due to its unique skull structure.
Stomatosuchus lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage. It likely inhabited the marshy lowlands of the modern-day Eastern Sahara Desert.
